newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end sharply off, silver firmer.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end sharply off, silver firmer.

text.p: Silver bucked the trend as all other New York precious metals settled sharply lower in generally thin volume ahead of Tuesday's Federal Reserve Open Market Committee which will mull an interest rate hike.
The market was also positioning itself for Tuesday's over-the-counter options expiry.
"Gold is probably going to stay in a tight range - there seems to be good support around $350 an ounce, but I don't see it going anywhere," a dealer said.
COMEX April gold settled $2.60 weaker at $350.40 an ounce.
April gold was traded $351.60 to $349.40 an ounce. June gold, soon to be most active, went out $2.90 lower at $353.00 an ounce.
COMEX gold volume was estimated at a modest 40,000 lots.
Bullion was quoted at $349.75/$350.25 an ounce by dealers.
Some dealers said the market had already factored in a rate hike Tuesday, but if there is a rise, gold may bounce a little.
David Rinehimer of Smith Barney said although a rate hike was usually not good for gold, if stocks or bonds reacted negatively to any hike, the yellow metal may glean some support.
"The market is reduced to an industrial metal at this point," a bullion trader commented.
Monday's gold volume was thin and largely involved a test of support in the spot market and some play surrounding Tuesday's options expiry, Rinehimer said.
Dealers said comments by Swiss National Bank chairman Hans Meyer may also have had a dampening effect on gold.
Meyer was quoted as saying that the primary goal was to decouple the currency from gold, although the proposed evaluation of gold reserves was a one-off measure for a long time to come.
A modest gain in silver was not seen as particularly significant by dealers.
COMEX May silver went out 3.2 cents firmer at $5.197 an ounce, traded $5.21 to $5.12. Volume was estimated at 11,000 lots.
COMEX gold stocks Monday fell 622 ounces to 774,512 ounces, while COMEX silver stocks fell 429,335 ounces to 191,819,471 ounces.
NYMEX April platinum ended lower on unconfirmed talk of a Russian shipment of metal finally arriving in Switzerland, as well as being pulled down by weakness in gold, dealers said.
April platinum went out $3.80 an ounce weaker at $378.50, while June NYMEX palladium settled $5.05 lower at $149.25 an ounce.
The U.S. government stockpile on Monday accepted bids for its first sale of surplus palladium and platinum.
(Huw Jones, New York Commodity Desk 212-859-1646))
